runs.t: An operation is idempotent when applying it more than once has the same intended effect as applying it once. In distributed applications it makes retries safe despite ambiguous network outcomes.

Use request-scoped idempotency keys, deduplication stores and atomic association of a result with its key. Define retention, payload mismatch behavior and concurrency. HTTP method labels alone do not ensure implementation correctness.
A client retries a card payment after timeout. Reusing its idempotency key must return the original outcome, not issue a second charge, even if the first response was lost.

Exactly-once effects across arbitrary components are difficult; most systems build at-least-once delivery plus idempotent processing. Keys reused with different requests must not silently produce misleading results.

Ask an agent to implement an idempotent payment endpoint with persistence-backed keys. Test duplicate requests, concurrent races, different payloads and process restart.
